text.t33: Matter analysis for claims, disputes and investigations
text.t35: The first draft of the case, in minutes
text.t36: Cicero reads the record the way your best junior would, if your best junior never slept. It separates facts from allegations, assertions and opinion, ties each one to the issues in dispute, and drafts the work product your team would otherwise build by hand. Every line can be checked against its source.
text.t40: From the day a production lands to the morning of the hearing.
text.t43: Hot documents flagged as the production lands
text.t45: The other side's case theory tested against their own documents
text.t48: Every allegation matched to each party's response

text.t50: The issues in dispute, set out for the team
text.t53: Event timelines drawn from the whole record

text.t84: Every document read by a person. Relevance found by luck and stamina.

text.t97: Every document read. Each fact pulled out, grouped into events and tied to the issues, with conflicting accounts flagged. The case is the output.
text.t99: Every fact, filed where it belongs
text.t100: A witness statement isn't one thing. It's dozens of claims about who did what, and when. Cicero pulls out each one, works out which event it describes and which issue it goes to, and checks it against everything else the record says about that event.
text.t106: Turns the allegations and denials into a list of what is actually in dispute, and who is involved.
text.t109: Breaks each document into its claims: who said what, when, where and to whom.
text.t112: Groups claims about the same event, wherever they came from. When two accounts disagree, you see both.
text.t115: Drafts the chronology, the issues and evidence matrices and the cast list, with a source on every line.
text.t117: The Agent works from that structure, not a keyword index, so its answers draw on the whole record and every citation opens at the paragraph it relies on.
text.t119: Every issue, and where the evidence lands
text.t120: One page per dispute that tells you where you stand. The Agent reads it before it answers anything.

text.t274: Cicero sits between the tools you already own
text.t275: Your eDiscovery platform holds and produces the record. Your firm-wide AI drafts and researches. Cicero is where the case gets built, in between.

text.t303: Analysis is no longer a step. It runs beneath every stage
text.t304: EDRM 2.0 (2025) restructures the industry-standard e-Discovery Reference Model. Analysis is no longer one step between processing and review. It is a continuous layer beneath every stage.
text.t305: Cicero is built for that layer. It turns the record into the matter map and the work product while review is still under way, not after it.
